Wetnose Raids

By: Bernadette Maguire | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Terrified hybrid wolf dogs, filth, sickly and dead dogs are the collateral damage of yet another puppy mill.

Summary:
Our animal shelters are overflowing, millions of dogs are put down unwanted around the world and yet the backyard breeders and puppy mills keep churning out a constant stream of puppies. Without them and more control there'd be a lot less unwanted animals in the world.

We go with Wetnose on a raid of 2 properties in Mpumalanga where hybrid wolves and other dogs are being bred in filthy conditions with little in the way of shelter or proper facilities. Most of them kept in small cages, they pace up and down, their stress palpable. Even the owner is unable to get close to them - they are terrified of humans.

In another case in the same week a top South African horse judge had 14 horses confiscated that were badly neglected and starving.

In both these cases the owners should have known better.

Further information:
A reality style, emotional roller coaster - as we join the raid and ask why people do this?

Visuals Script

VO: 17”
It was an unusual scene outside the Delmas police station in Mpumalanga on Tuesday afternoon - a cavalcade of Wetnose bakkies and trailers , supported by the local SPCA had gathered. We were joining them on a raid of a local puppy mill outside town. Inspector Jacques van der Merwe had secured a warrant to search and seize on the property. (30:50)

Jacques:
The complaint was regarding the breeder on the farm. I went out this morning to have a look and I was actually shocked by the condition of some of those dogs kept in those conditions.

Devi: Was it bad?

Jacques: Ja so I came to the magistrate and I showed her the pictures and she immediately said its safer to get the warrant.

VO: 8”
Once we were on route with our police escort Jacques explained what he’d seen that morning.

Drop in pictures – cell phone ones dirty cages Jacques:
Went out this morning – I was shocked…dirty water bowls, dirty living conditions. For a long time I have not seen it this bad of breeding going on.

VO: 8”
Driving into the property no-one would guess that this was a puppy mill. Sarah Penning who lives on the property – came out to meet us.

Jacques: Who is looking after the animals on the property?

Sarah: I am – I’ve just gotten a guy in now to help me on the property.

Jacques: Since when is he here?

Sarah:
This afternoon. I’ve just gotten the guy in now to assist me.

Jacques: So it’s the first time he’s here cleaning the kennels?

Sarah: Yes

Jacques: Mam that is a problem in terms of the Animal Protection Act.

Sarah: Ja of course yes but I haven’t had the funds or anything – I’ve just moved here.

Jacques: Mam that’s no excuse – if you cannot afford to have them like this it is a problem.

Sarah:
Well I’m busy sorting it out you can go and have a look at everything.

VO:10”
One of the first discoveries that was made was this exercise chain on the front lawn – its commonly used for sled dog training – an outlawed practice in South Africa.

Jacques:
Can I go with you and show you what the problems are and what is the Animal Protection Act stating against that? I mean you are a month here – even if you don’t use that training chain why do you leave it there?

Sarah: You can see I haven’t even cut the grass – I have done nothing.

Jacques: Then that means there is nothing done with the animals.

VO: 3”
Sarah claimed she wasn’t a breeder.

And refused to show us around.

Devi:
But to be fair to you show us where there is no problem – because you don’t think there is a problem.

Sarah:
No I didn’t say there’s no problem – I’m dealing with the problems as they come along.


VO: 9”
Walking into the back garden we soon realized these were not ordinary dogs. In a small cage a wolf dog paced relentlessly – showing signs of distress.

Jacques:
You see, they don’t even come here properly, you have to struggle to get this gate open. It’s dirty – it’s not even clean.

VO: 7”
In a kennel next door were three more wolf hybrids. The dogs cowered away and Jacques became visibly emotional.

Jacques:
Dogs that appear to be very emaciated, scared. Areas where dogfood is lying where they are sleeping not ideal.

VO: 22”
Hastily, food had clearly been put out in anticipation of our visit. Dotted all over were cages full of wolf hybrids and puppy’s in similar filthy conditions. On the outskirts of the property was a deserted outbuilding. Here we found dogs caged and puppy’s barricaded in with no shelter.

Debbie:
There is no shelter – there is no roof on here – so they are sleeping in the rain. Look at all the water here that is vrotting and green.

VO: 2
One of them appeared to be injured.

Jacques:
It’s his leg. His leg is sore.

VO:
Frightened he limped away.

Devi link:
How somebody thought that this was okay completely boggles my mind…but there’s more to see.

VO: 4:
Then in a farm dam adjacent we made a gruesome discovery.

Devi: No Man!

Jacques:
This is very disgusting…dead dogs, dead rats…chickens…dead everything. Dog faeces, everything they…that’s a dog’s leg. Ja.So

VO: 10””
Dog fur and even a skull were visible amongst the discarded remains. Alongside sat a bucket of rotting chickens – ostensibly the dog’s food.


VO: 5”
Everywhere we turned we were met with more horror discoveries.

Devi link
So two dogs have been found inside this trailer on the property.

VO: 3”
One of them was virtually lifeless.

Devi:

Hey baby, hey….how man?

VO: 9”
Clearly this dog was in urgent need of medical attention. One of the staff on the property told us the dogs had been hidden.

Veronica:
Devi I think we have one bilary case here.

Debbie: Has she got bilary? Oh and she’s been injured. That’s why she’s been hidden away neh.

VO: 7”
In the interim Sarah started peering at us from the outskirts. We decided to confront her.

Devi:
Sarah can you explain to me why you’ve got dead dogs there? And why did you lock up those other dogs? Can you explain that to us? Why are you running away?

Sarah:
F- off!

Devi: Sorry what did you say?

Sarah:
I said f- off!

Shorten don’t show the house…. VO: 33”
She disappeared back into her house and locked herself in. Jacques and his team started gathering up the dogs for confiscation. They loaded them in trailers but some proved harder to catch than others.










Pic of Danie Opperman
And in the midst of trying to catch them – Sarah bid a hasty retreat. The team tried in vain to lure this terrified wolf hybrid and eventually had to give up and head back to the kennels with the confiscated dogs some of whom had to be sedated.

The next morning we found ourselves back outside a police station, this time in the adjacent suburb of Eloff – where we believed the Sarah’s partner in the breeding operation, Danie Opperman was based.

Jacques:
It’s the same breeder that we went yesterday to collect some dogs from so we might expect some real odd bad looking cases if anything is compared to the ones from yesterday…

VO: 12”
On arrival Danie Opperman refused to let our cameras in so we filmed from behind the perimeter wall.

Add in photos VO: 10”
From outside we watched the team’s progress around the property. Again there were wolf hybrids and another rare breed called Euro hounds. Jacques found a gravesite which Danie claimed were dogs poisoned with 2 step. There was also a dog with a broken leg that had not been treated and it grew back skew. Several of the dogs had untreated wounds like this little maltese. It didn’t take long to see why – fights were an all too regular occurrence among his 50 dogs.

7:00

longer VO:
Conditions were better but still out of control.

Jacques:
There’s a couple of dogs here in the back that’s not in a very good condition so we are going to take them as well as most of the dogs on these premises.

Cellphone
VO:21
In makeshift conditions we found a terrified breeding bitch and we filmed Danie on a cell phone for several minutes trying to catch this beautiful German Short haired pointer bitch. Eventually he gave up.

Jacques
A dog shouldn’t be – if you look after your animal should not be that afraid of you – that means really that there was no interaction with those animals they were not used to human contact.

VO:
In terms of the warrant they had to take all the dogs – Danie had no option.

Jacques:
We had a look at the circumstances. The law states very clearly in terms of the Animal Protection Act as well as the warrant is to examine these animals and to prevent further suffering is to remove those animals out of that care until the investigation can be finalized as well as the court finalise the matter.

Debbie:
And all in all it added up now to close to close on a hundred dogs.

VO: 6”
Breeding with dogs with these dogs would just mean more dogs in shelters down the line.

Jacques:
The dogs are emotionally traumatised because they do not get the treatment that they should have in human interaction.

VO: 10”
Back at Wetnose the dogs are all in kennels. Some of them were in need of urgent veterinary care. Like the dog we found in the trailer.

Debbie:
This one has very bad tick bite fever, the other one also had tick bite fever and a wound on its leg.

VO: 5
And the puppy with the sore leg – well it was a bit more serious….

Debbie:
We’ve actually found that he had a broken leg that was untreated for quite a long time.

VO:
Apart from which he was severely malnourished.

Debbie:
Feel that- he’s so skinny. You can’t see it the hair just hides it well. Feel his spine that is so skinny. His spine is sticking out all the way along there - you can even count the ribs.

VO: 6
Another one of the house dogs rescued from Danie’s property had new and old wounds on his neck.

Upsound
This dog has definitely been denied veterinary care and its gross neglect.

VO: 7”
Veronica will now have to start the slow process of rehabilating some of these dogs.

Veronica:
You need to earn their trust – so I will go every day and just sit with them and see if they will trust me in time.

.



VO: 5
It’s the collateral damage that backyard breeders cause in pursuit of money.

Debbie:
They start out with good intentions and it starts to get out of hand. To raise puppies correctly and give them all their vaccinations, give them the right type of food gets expensive and then money becomes an issue. The animals become more and more and the money gets less and less and the money that they are making out of selling the puppies is used to live off and doesn’t go back into the welfare of the animals.

longer VO:
And now that the dogs are safe the investigation into breeders Danie Opperman and Sarah Penning’s operation needs to start. It looks like they will have a lot to answer for.

Jacques:
We are in the process now of going to the police station and opening a formal docket against Mr Opperman and charge him and everyone on the property at the time, on both premises with cruelty to animals.

VO: 10
2 raids on puppy mills where dogs and wolves are fed rotting chickens and live in filthy conditions without shelter, veterinary care or human contact. They’re just breeding machines.

Debbie:
I think we have a case of bilary here – that’s why she was hidden away./Gross neglect one.
